subject: Recap + numbers: Finthrive discovery (token economics & pilot proposal)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Cara Nguyen <cara@finthrive.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + numbers: Finthrive discovery (token economics & pilot proposal)

Hi Cara — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have alignment on pain points, the levers we discussed, and proposed next steps. I put a couple of rough attachments on cost scenarios (see below).

Key pain points you shared
- Unpredictable inference spend month-to-month as customers burst and we lack request-level batching and session caching.
- 95/99th latency spikes on our short-turn prompts (templates + structured slots) are impacting UX and conversion. Target is ~<250ms P99.
- Current infra budget for model inference is ~USD 10k–12k / month (hard ceiling during FY26 pilot). Any solution needs to show clear cost benefits or payback within one quarter.

What we confirmed on the call
- Typical workload: ~150M tokens/month today (50% prompts are short, <40 tokens; 25% are long session continuations that reuse context).
- Peak concurrency: short spikes up to ~200 reqs/sec during business hours.
- Other constraints: data residency in us-east for logging, SOC2 compliance required for production.

Redwood levers and rough economics (ballpark):
- Batching & request coalescing: can reduce per-token compute by ~20–35% for short prompts by grouping small requests into continuous batches during micro-spikes.
- Prefix/KV caching for session continuations: expected 15–30% token savings by reusing KV cache and avoiding full recomputation for repeated context.
- Quantized model variants: 2x–3x cost reduction on GPU inference with small latency changes; good fit for read-heavy/embeddings-heavy stages.

Baseline rough numbers (illustrative only)
- Current estimated spend on your existing hosted model: ~USD 18k/month (no batching, conservative per-token rate).
- Redwood hosted (apply batching + cache): estimated USD 9k–11k/month.
- Redwood Dedicated (8×GPU reserved + autoscale buffer): estimated committed price ~USD 7k–9k/month (with 12-month commit discount).

Next steps we agreed
1) I will send a short, conservative ROI worksheet with two scenarios (hosted pilot, 30-day proof with a cost cap; and dedicated reserved option). Attached: 20260220-finthrive-rough-roi.xlsx and redwood-token-econ-one-pager.pdf.
2) Technical deep-dive with Vivek to validate latency numbers, batching feasibility, and KV caching on a sample of your traffic (30–60 minutes). Vivek, can we target next Tue morning PT?
3) Procurement contact (if comfortable) — Ben, if you could loop in procurement and let us know required contract terms / PO cadence, we can share a pilot SOW and a DocuSign-ready proposal.

If anything above is off, flag it and I will update. Thanks again — Aisha

--
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0112

Date: Fri, 21 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + numbers: Finthrive discovery (token economics & pilot proposal)

Thanks Aisha — helpful recap and the ROI one-pager looks useful. A few quick clarifications from our side before the pilot SOW: 

- Token counts: our current run-rate is closer to 150M tokens/month (I rounded in the call). Of that, about 60% are short prompts (<=40 tokens).
- Budget: the execution team has a hard budget cap of USD 10k/month for the pilot phase. We can discuss committed spend for dedicated later if the pilot proves out.
- Latency: P99 goal is 250ms for the vast majority of short prompts — we may accept slightly higher for long continuations.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II reports and an IP/data handling attestation are required to move to production.

Can you provide two concrete line-item estimates (hosted pilot with a 30-day cap and a dedicated 8-GPU committed scenario) that show: 1) pre/post batching & caching cost, 2) expected latency P50/P99, 3) any startup/engineering effort estimate (hours) for integrating prefix caching.

Looping Ben from procurement to make sure contract cadence is visible; Ben — what's your preferred procurement timeline for pilots (PO vs. credit card)?

Thanks — Cara

Great — thanks for the clarifications, Cara. Below are the two concrete, conservative scenarios you asked for. These are intentionally simple so procurement can review quickly; I can follow up with a more detailed CSV breakout if useful (I attached one).

Scenario A — Hosted pilot (30-day proof, capped)
- Assumptions: 150M tokens/month pro-rated to 30 days (approx 5M tokens), batching & KV caching enabled during pilot targeting conservative 20% token-reduction. Model: quantized open model variant (latency-optimized).
- Costs: baseline hosted per-token (no optimizations) = baseline estimate $0.0036 per 1k tokens
  * Baseline monthly (no optim): ~USD 540 (for pilot-sized 5M tokens)
  * With batching + caching (-20% tokens) = ~USD 432
  * Add pilot support & monitoring uplift (flat): USD 1,000 one-time during pilot
  => Estimated pilot month spend (hosted): USD 1,432 (capped by agreement, we can set cap at USD 2,000).
- Latency expectation: P50 ~60–80ms; P99 ~190–260ms for short prompts (depends on end-to-end network and telemetry).
- Integration effort: ~8–12 engineering hours to add request coalescing hooks and enable prefix caching for the pilot.

Scenario B — Dedicated reserved (8×GPU pool, monthly commit)
- Assumptions: committed throughput for steady-state 150M tokens/month with room for 2x micro-spike bursts; batch-friendly runtime; quantized runtime enabled.
- Costs: committed reserved monthly fee (after standard enterprise discount) = USD 7,500–9,000 / month.
- Latency expectation: P50 ~45–65ms; P99 ~120–200ms for short prompts with aggressive batching and KV caching.
- Integration effort: ~16–32 engineering hours for production hardening, metrics integration, and privacy attestation work (SOC2 evidence pipeline).

ROI framing (very conservative)
- If we reduce inference unit cost by ~40% and improve P99 to <200ms, your product team estimates a 10–15% lift in conversion on targeted flows. For Finthrive, a conservative 10% lift at current ARR run-rate would offset the incremental committed cost within ~2–3 quarters. I can run a model-specific ROI calculation if you share LTV/ARPU for the conversion cohort.

Attachments: detailed-scenario-costing-20260220.csv (per your request)

Next suggested steps
- Approve a hosted 30-day pilot (cap USD 2,000) so we can validate real traffic savings and latency on your sample.
- Schedule the technical deep-dive with Vivek for next Tue / Wed. Vivek — can you confirm availability?
- Ben — if procurement prefers PO for pilots, tell us the PO terms and we will produce a short SOW + DocuSign link.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Aisha

--

Hi all — quick tech note ahead of the deep-dive:

- Batching feasibility: for your 60% short-prompt mix, we can safely apply continuous micro-batching with virtually zero changes to the client (just a middleware coalescer or our SDK). Expected 20–30% compute reduction on short prompts in production, higher at peak if you allow 10–50ms extra micro-queueing.
- KV/prefix caching: we'll need a short sample of session traces (anonymized) — 2k–5k sessions — to estimate realistic cache hit rates. Typical customers with similar session patterns see 15–28% token savings.
- P99 latency levers: colocating inference in us-east and using our low-latency networking path is key. For Dedicated we can hit target 250ms P99 with our recommended config.

For the deep-dive, please share a short sample (S3 link or anonymized csv) and I will run a quick sizing run and latency simulation. I can be available Tue 10–11am PT or Wed 9–10am PT — which works for you?

-Vivek
